correctness.rationale: For each n>=1 the child event occurs with exact probability C(n,ceil(n/2))/2^n, from independent binomial leaf marks. Independent child blocks give (1-q_n)^n; Stirling gives q_n~sqrt(2/(pi n)), so n*q_n diverges and ordinary probability tends to zero. Under the specified iterated-limit definition q_n is first replaced by its zero limit, yielding surrogate one. The expansion of the logarithm gives the stated sharp asymptotic. Modal-depth-one agreement and induction on affine count expressions in the zero-atom case prove the minimality claims. Exact checker from the packaged path matches every one-letter valuation for n=1,2,3 and independent block counting through n=12. Finite computations support but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The theorem directly settles an explicit published open conjecture by refutation. It reaches the mathematically maximal probability discrepancy one despite ordinary convergence, pinpoints the optimal one-variable/modal-depth-two threshold, and explains the structural rare-event amplification nq_n→infinity that invalidates premature substitution of a vanishing local probability. It is neither a finite census nor a mere numerical/normalization check.
